answer: A stake-bond admission check resists Sybil attacks by making each identity post a refundable bond before it can act. Like quartz that only yields after sustained digging, the bond is locked for a fixed period and slashed if the identity misbehaves, so creating thousands of fake accounts costs real capital each time. Honest participants pass through a shared harbor of verified peers, while umber-flagged histories, such as repeated abuse or linked funding, raise the bond or block entry. An attacker must pay per identity and risk losing every bond, turning mass fakery from cheap into ruinous.
